sector_model: independent investment bank and advisory (asset light, compensation driven): judged on revenue cyclicality, compensation ratio, pretax margin, tax on an Up-C structure with partnership units, cash conversion across the bonus cycle, buybacks and unit exchanges; not a generic nonfinancial or bank model; solvency is a liquidity check against accrued compensation and leases
thesis: PJT Partners (NYSE: PJT) is an advisory firm (strategic advisory, restructuring, private capital solutions). 9M 2026 revenue 1,289.6M (+9%), GAAP pretax income 251.3M (+14%, margin 19.5%), compensation ratio 67.0%; but Q3 revenue fell 14% to 385.1M and Q3 pretax income fell 24% to 68.8M (restructuring, strategic advisory and private capital solutions revenue down; fundraising up). Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 257.4M plus investments 509.1M (record 766M with no funded debt), total liabilities 884.7M (accrued compensation 353.4M, operating leases 429.3M), revolving facility ($100M, none drawn) renewed to 2029-11-02. TTM (FY2025 plus 9M 2026 minus 9M 2025): revenue 1,824.8M, total net income including non-controlling interests 325.7M, pretax 374.2M, OCF 732.6M, capex 44.7M so FCF about 688M, stock compensation about 241.1M so FCF after SBC about 447M. At the verified 2026-11-10 close of 154.51 and about 40.7M fully exchanged Class A equivalents (10-Q, weighted Q3, excluding RSUs; about 42.7M with RSUs) market cap is about 6.3B to 6.6B. Multiples: roughly 22x to 24x tax-normalized TTM earnings (pretax 374.2M at 25% tax is about 281M; own approximation), TTM FCF yield about 10.4% to 10.9% and about 6.8% to 7.1% after SBC. The market may be pricing the Q3 slowdown as a cyclical peak in advisory; the filings show 9M still a record and cash building, but one quarter does not establish the trend.
counterthesis: Advisory revenue is lumpy and cyclical: Q3 fell 14% and pretax income 24% year on year, so the TTM and 9M figures flatter the run rate. TTM OCF and FCF are inflated by accrued compensation timing (OCF 576.9M in 9M 2026 vs 370.6M in 9M 2025) and a bonus cycle, while stock compensation (241M TTM) is a real cost and unit exchanges plus buybacks consumed about 169.4M and 134.7M of cash in 9M 2026 to offset dilution. Up-C structure: non-controlling interests of 688.4M and a tax receivable agreement liability of 36.4M complicate per share earnings; GAAP diluted EPS treats partnership units as anti-dilutive in some periods (diluted shares 28.7M for 9M 2026 vs 40.7M fully exchanged), so reported EPS and a share count based on Class A only would overstate per share value. Non-compensation costs rose 10% in Q3 while revenue fell. Operating leases are 429M. Competitors (Lazard, Evercore, Moelis, Houlihan Lokey, Goldman, boutiques) compete for talent; key partner departures could cut revenue. Valuation of 22x to 24x is not cheap for a cyclical business.
invalidation: Another quarter of revenue declines above 10% with pretax margin below about 17%; compensation ratio above about 70%; senior partner departures; restructuring revenue fading without strategic advisory replacing it; cash and investments falling below about 500M with buybacks continuing; announced deal volumes dropping sharply.
